building.name: Matson Building
building.completed_conflict: The dates on record for the Matson Building disagree: this page carries 1921, the 2008 Transit Center survey dates the building on the parcel to 1922, and the city's statement on Progressive Era and early revival styles gives 1923 in its text and 1922-1924 in its illustration caption.

historic_survey.status_code_meaning: California Historical Resource Status Codes: a 1 or 2 means listed or formally determined eligible, a 3 means the survey judged it eligible, a 4 that it may become eligible, a 6 that it was found ineligible, and a 7 that it was not evaluated.
historic_survey.note: Listed in the National Register of Historic Places. Recorded as an individually significant building. The survey prints this building's address two ways: 215 Market Street in one table and 245 Market Street in another.

historic_survey.note: Two buildings on this parcel, each named as a Chicago School example: the Matson Building at 215 Market Street, designed by Bliss & Faville, and the PG&E General Office Building at 245 Market Street, designed by Bakewell & Brown.
